<entry id="S01002">
<head-word>קִימָה</head-word>
<pos> f.</pos>
<language-key>(b. h.;</language-key>
<language-reference>
<xref rid="A00083"> קוּם)</xref></language-reference>
<senses>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>standing up, rising</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Ber. 11
<sup>a</sup> (expl. ובקומך, Deut. VI, 7) בשעת ק' ק' ממש at the time of rising, whereby rising in its proper sense is meant (rising from bed, and not in the sense of standing erect at recital). Kidd. 32
<sup>b</sup> (ref. to Lev. XIX, 3</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>2)</number>
<definition> לא אמרתי ק' אלא וכ' the text means only the rising that is a token of respect, v. 
<xref rid="E00344">הִידּוּר</xref>.</definition>
<notes> Ib. מה ק' שאין בה וכ' as rising is something with which no material sacrifice is connected &c. Ib. 33
<sup>a</sup>, v. בִּיטּוּל; a. fr.—2) 
<italic>erection, putting up</italic>. Y. Ab. Zar. IV, 44
<sup>a</sup> (ref. to Lev. XXVI, 1) לא היא עשייה לא היא ק' are ‘making’ and ‘erecting’ not the same? Answ. עשייה בתחילה ק' וכ', v. עֲשִׂיָּה; a. e.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="S01024">
<head-word>קִינָה</head-word>
<pos> f.</pos>
<language-key>(b. h.;</language-key>
<language-reference>
<xref rid="A00083"> קוּן)</xref></language-reference>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> [
<italic>rhythmic song</italic> (v. P. Sm. 3603 s. v. קינא),] 
<italic>lamentation, dirge</italic>.</definition>
<notes> M. Kat. III, 9 ק' שאחת מדברת וכ' a lamentation is called 
<italic>ḳinah</italic>, when one speaks &c., v. עִינּוּי I. Ber. 7
<sup>b</sup> (ref. to Ps. III, </notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition> מזמור … ק' וכ' ‘a song of David’? it ought to read, ‘a lamentation of David.</definition>
<notes>’ Lam. R. to IV, 11 (ref. to Ps. LXXIX, 1) לא הוה קרא … בכי … נהי … ק' לאסף the text ought to read, ‘a weeping of Asaf’, ‘an elegy of Asaf’, ‘a lamentation of Asaf’. Ib. introd., end (ref. to Jer. IX, 9) על נאותיו … שנהפכו לק' over the beauties (pleasures) of Jacob which have been changed into mourning; a. fr.—[Gitt. 58
<sup>a</sup> ועליהן קינה, v. קוּן.]—
<plural-form>Pl. קִינוֹת,</plural-form> esp. ספר ק', מגילת ק', or ק' 
<italic>the Book of Lamentations</italic>. B. Bath. 14
<sup>b</sup> סדרן … ק' וכ' the order of the books of Hagiographa is: Ruth … and Lamentations &c. Ib. 15
<sup>a</sup> ירמיה … וקנות (corr. acc.) Jeremiah composed the book that bears his name, the Book of Kings, and Lamentations. Ḥag. 5
<sup>b</sup> רבי … ספר ק' Rabbi took up the Book of Lamentations and read &c. Y. Sabb. XVI, 15
<sup>c</sup> top היו … במגילת ק' were sitting and explaining the scroll of Lamentations; Lam. R. to IV, 20; Lev. R. s. 15; 
<pgbrk id="pg1363" />a. e.—Y. Pes. VIII, end, 36
<sup>b</sup>; Y. M. Kat. I, 80
<sup>d</sup> top קִינִים ונהי lamentations and elegies.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="S01027">
<head-word>קִינּוּי</head-word>
<head-word>קִנּ'</head-word>
<pos> m.</pos>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (קָנָא) 
<italic>manifestation of jealousy, warning given to the suspected wife</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Sot. 2
<sup>b</sup> (ref. to Mish. I, 1, ‘he must warn her in the presence of two witnesses’) אמר קרא בה ולא בק' the text (Num. V, 13) says, 
<italic>bah</italic> (there is no witness to it) that is to say, 
<italic>to it</italic> (her defilement) one witness would suffice, but not to her warning. Ib. ק' על פי עצמו the act may be certified by the husband’s own testimony; ק' על פי שנים two witnesses must testify to &c. Ib. 3
<sup>a</sup> אין ק' … התראה 
<italic>ḳinnuy</italic> means warning (in the presence of two witnesses). Y. ib. I, beg. 16
<sup>b</sup> הק' … חובה וכ' to warn is the husband’s duty; R. J. says, it is optional. Ib. קִינּוּיוֹ ק' a warning (under such conditions) is legally valid; a. fr.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="S01029">
<head-word>קִינוֹנְיָא</head-word>
<head-word>קְנוֹ'</head-word>
<pos> f.</pos>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (κοινωνία) 
<italic>partnership</italic>; (used in an evil sense) 
<italic>conspiracy to defraud and divide the profits</italic>.</definition>
<notes> B. Bath. X, 7 (173
<sup>b</sup>) הערב … שמא יעשו קינ' וכ' Y. ed. a. Bab. (Mish. ed. קנ') if one has become surety to a woman for her jointure, and her husband divorces her, the husband must vow that he will never accept any benefit from her (so that he cannot remarry her), lest they form a conspiracy against the guarantor’s property and (after collecting the jointure) he take his wife back. Y. B. Mets. I, end, 8
<sup>a</sup> a note of indebtedness found must not he returned מפני ק' because a conspiracy may be formed (between the creditor and the debtor to collect the debt, already cancelled, from the purchaser of the debtor’s land, v. לְקוּחוֹת); Bab. ib. 13
<sup>a</sup> חייש לפרעון ולק' (Abayi forbids the restoration of the note, because) he apprehends that it may have been paid, and a conspiracy may be formed; לא חיישינן … וק' we do not apprehend &c. Tosef. Kidd. III, 5 על מנת … שמא עשו ק' if one says to a woman, be betrothed unto me on the condition that …: she is betrothed, because we apprehend a conspiracy (between them to annul the betrothal without a formal Geṭ); a. e.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="S01030">
<head-word>קִינוֹף</head-word>
<head-word>קִינּוֹף</head-word>
<pos> m.</pos>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (קנף, sec. r. of קף, cmp. צִינוֹק, צִנּוֹר &c.; an adaptation of κωνωπεῖον) 
<italic>the framework of a baldachin</italic> or 
<italic>canopy</italic>, consisting of four columns over which a flat cover is spread, contrad. to נַקְלִיטִין.</definition>
<notes> Succ. I, 3 (10
<sup>a</sup>) או שפירס ע"ג ק' (not שפירסה) or if he spread a sheet over a frame (so as to form a tent within the Succah); ib. 10
<sup>b</sup> Ms. M. (ed. קינופות). Snh. 68
<sup>a</sup> הוא יושב בק' שלו he was seated on his curtained couch.—
<plural-form>Pl. קִינוֹפוֹת, קִינּ'</plural-form>. Succ. l. c. וק' ארבעה, v. נַקְלִיטִין. Ib. שאני ק' דקביעי it is different with baldachin frames, for they are stationary, opp. to כִּילָה. Tosef. Kel. B. Mets. II, 8.—[Κωνωπεῖον means the 
<italic>net</italic>, our w. refers to the 
<italic>frame</italic>.]</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="S01035">

<definition> (קִנְטֵר) 
<italic>opposition, remonstrance; reproach</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Yalk. Ex. 241 קִינְטוּרוֹ באז his (Moses’) remonstrance is introduced with אָז (Ex. V, 23).—

Ib. דברים ק' (insert של or read: דברי) reproachful words, opp. נִחוּמִים; (Ar. a. Yalk. Jer. 265 קִנְתּוּרִין). Koh.
